title: Tourist Information
description: Four short recordings for visitors to a town: a tourist office, a bus tour, asking for directions and a museum message.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer (A, B or C) for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · At the tourist office
parts.intro: You will hear a tourist, Linh, talking to a clerk, Henry, at a tourist information centre.

script.speaker: Henry
script.text: Good morning. Welcome to the Lakeside Tourist Information Centre. How can I help you?

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Hi. We're here for three days, and we'd like some ideas for things to do.

script.speaker: Henry
script.text: Of course. Are you interested in history, or do you prefer outdoor activities?

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: My husband loves history, but I'd rather be outside. And we have a nine-year-old daughter.

script.speaker: Henry
script.text: Then I'd suggest the castle for the morning. Children love it because there's a small dragon museum inside. Then in the afternoon you could hire a boat on the lake.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: A boat sounds lovely. How much is it?

script.speaker: Henry
script.text: Twelve pounds an hour for a small boat. It's cheaper after four o'clock, only eight pounds.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Great. And is the castle open on Mondays?

script.speaker: Henry
script.text: No, I'm afraid it's closed on Mondays, but it's open every other day from ten until five.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Today is Monday, so we'll go to the lake today, and the castle tomorrow.

script.speaker: Henry
script.text: Good plan. Here's a free map. The castle is just a twenty-minute walk from here.

parts.title: Part 2 · A bus tour
parts.intro: You will hear a guide, Frank, at the start of a sightseeing bus tour.

script.speaker: Frank
script.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome aboard the City Sightseer bus. My name is Frank and I'll be your guide today.

script.speaker: Frank
script.text: The tour lasts one hour and fifteen minutes, and you can get off at any of the eight stops and catch the next bus. Your ticket is valid for twenty-four hours.

script.speaker: Frank
script.text: On your left, you can see the Town Hall. It was built about two hundred years ago, and it's still used today. The clock tower is a favourite place for photos.

script.speaker: Frank
script.text: In a few minutes, we'll pass the old market. It's open every day except Sunday, and it's a great place to buy local cheese and bread. Please try the apple cake. It's famous!

script.speaker: Frank
script.text: After that, we cross the river on the Green Bridge. Many people think it's the most beautiful bridge in the country, but actually, it's quite new. It was finished only ten years ago.

script.speaker: Frank
script.text: Please remember to keep your arms inside the bus when we go under low trees, and take care of your bags. Next stop: the castle.

parts.title: Part 3 · Asking for directions
parts.intro: You will hear a tourist, Minh, asking a local woman, Mrs Hill, for directions.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: Excuse me, could you help me? I'm looking for the Museum of Science.

script.speaker: Mrs Hill
script.text: Of course. It's not far. Go straight on along this road until you reach the traffic lights.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: Straight on to the traffic lights. OK.

script.speaker: Mrs Hill
script.text: Then turn left, and walk past the post office and the big supermarket. The museum is opposite the park.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: Is it a long way? I've got a heavy bag.

script.speaker: Mrs Hill
script.text: About ten minutes on foot. But there's also a bus, number twelve. It stops outside the supermarket, and it's only one pound.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: I think I'll walk. It's a lovely day.

script.speaker: Mrs Hill
script.text: Be careful, though. The museum closes at four today, not five, because of a school event.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: Oh, thanks. It's half past three now, so I only have half an hour.

script.speaker: Mrs Hill
script.text: Then take the bus! Or you could come back tomorrow. It's free on Wednesdays.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: Free? That's great. But I leave tomorrow. I'll go by bus now, then.

parts.title: Part 4 · A recorded message
parts.intro: You will hear a recorded telephone message from a museum.

script.speaker: Museum
script.text: Thank you for calling Greenfield Museum. This is a recorded message.

script.speaker: Museum
script.text: The museum is open from Tuesday to Sunday, from half past nine in the morning until five in the evening. We are closed on Mondays. On the last Friday of every month, we stay open until nine o'clock, and there is live music in the garden.

script.speaker: Museum
script.text: Tickets for adults are seven pounds fifty. Children under five can come in for free, and students pay half price. If you are over sixty-five, you can enter for five pounds.

script.speaker: Museum
script.text: This month, we have a special show about dinosaurs on the first floor. It will be here until the end of June. Tickets for the show cost three pounds extra.

script.speaker: Museum
script.text: Our café on the ground floor sells hot meals, sandwiches and ice cream. You can also bring your own lunch and eat it in the garden if it's sunny.

script.speaker: Museum
script.text: For directions, please press one. To book a school visit, press two. To speak to someone, press three. Thank you.
